Performance

Source: vignettes/articles/performance.Rmd
performance.Rmd

A page of Element components takes longer to start than a page of Shiny’s own inputs. This article says where the time goes, what the package does about it, and the settings that make a page of many components start faster. The numbers were measured on a shared server (four CPUs, headless Chrome); a desktop is faster, but the proportions hold.

Where the time goes

Starting a page has three parts:

  1. The server writes the page. Each component is turned into its template and its options (JSON). The first page of a new R process also draws the page’s Bootstrap theme.
  2. The browser loads the libraries: Vue and Element Plus, about 620 KB, where a plain Shiny page loads about 240 KB.
  3. The browser draws each component. Every component is a Vue application of its own: its template is compiled and Element renders it. This is the part that grows with the number of components.
Page All components drawn
100 Shiny inputs 1.5 s
5 Element components 2.9 s
100 Element components 3.9 s
300 Element components 5.7 s

Most of the third part is Element rendering its own components, not Vue: 300 el-selects drawn by one Vue application take 3.2 s, by 300 applications 3.4 to 3.9 s. Some components cost far more than others (per component, in the browser):

Component Time
el_input() 0.5 ms
el_select() 11 ms
el_cascader() 8 ms
el_tree_select() 14 ms
el_date_picker() 14 ms
el_dropdown() 8 ms
el_popover() 4 ms

What the package does

  • The theme is drawn once per machine. bslib compiles a page’s theme in every new R process; el_page() takes it from sass’s cache instead, and the default el_theme() is shipped compiled, so even a machine that never drew it does not compile it. The first page of a new process takes about 0.3 s to write, as a plain Shiny page with a bslib theme does.
  • Each component is written in about 6 ms: its dependencies are made once per session and its options written by a JSON writer in C.
  • el_page() shows Element’s loading mask until every component is drawn and Shiny is connected, rather than a page that is not yet usable. el_page(loading = FALSE) leaves it out.

Components drawn later, by renderUI()

The loading mask covers the page as it opens. A uiOutput() whose renderUI() draws many components later goes through the same two parts, on its own:

renderUI() drawing Server done Components drawn
20 el_select()s 1.0 s 1.4 s
100 el_select()s 2.1 s 3.7 s
300 el_select()s 4.5 s 9.1 s

While the server computes, Shiny marks the output as recalculating (it fades). Shiny’s busy indicators show a spinner in the output instead – in the output only, not over the page:

el_page(
  shiny::useBusyIndicators(),
  uiOutput("area")
)

While the browser then draws the components, it can draw nothing else: a spinner stops turning until the last one is drawn. Draw fewer at once – persistent = FALSE below, or a virtual list – rather than more.

Drawing less at first

Element renders some parts of a component before they are needed, and offers options to render them only when they are. The package keeps Element’s defaults; set these where a page has many components.

Dropdowns drawn when opened: persistent = FALSE

A component with a dropdown or a popup renders it when the page loads, hidden, so that it opens at once (persistent = TRUE, Element’s default). With persistent = FALSE it is rendered the first time it opens – a few milliseconds then – and removed when it closes. For 100 components:

Component persistent = TRUE (default) persistent = FALSE
el_select() 1.1 s 0.18 s
el_tree_select() 1.4 s 0.25 s
el_cascader() 0.8 s 0.18 s
el_color_picker() 0.65 s 0.15 s
el_dropdown() 0.8 s 0.10 s
el_popover() 0.4 s 0.06 s
el_tooltip() 0.04 s 0.04 s

persistent is an argument of el_select(), el_select_v2(), el_tree_select(), el_cascader(), el_color_picker(), el_dropdown(), el_menu(), el_popconfirm(), el_popover(), el_slider() and el_tooltip(). el_date_picker() has no such option.

el_select("city", choices = cities, persistent = FALSE)

Content drawn when needed

Option Components What it does
render_after_expand el_tree(), el_tree_select() renders a node’s children when it is expanded (on by default)
lazy with the server loading el_tree(), el_cascader(), el_table() (tree rows) asks the server for a level when it is opened: see el_load_children()
lazy el_image() loads the picture when it scrolls into view
destroy_on_close el_dialog(), el_drawer() removes the content when closed

Long lists: virtual scrolling

These render only the rows in view, so ten thousand rows cost as little as a screenful:

  • el_select_v2() instead of el_select();
  • el_table_v2() instead of el_table();
  • el_tree_v2() instead of el_tree();
  • el_cascader(virtual_scroll = TRUE), el_transfer(virtual_scroll = TRUE).

Deploying an app with its own theme

A theme of your own is compiled once on each machine, then taken from sass’s cache. On a server – Posit Connect, shinyapps.io – sass keeps that cache in the app’s directory, app_cache/sass, when it exists. Run the app once locally with that directory created, and deploy it with the app:

dir.create("app_cache/sass", recursive = TRUE)
shiny::runApp() # draws the theme once into app_cache/sass
# then deploy, app_cache/ included

The default el_theme() needs none of this: the package ships it compiled.
